fastapi: In a default FastAPI app, which path serves the interactive Swagger UI documentation?
/docs
/swagger
/api-docs
/openapi
FastAPI serves Swagger UI at /docs and ReDoc at /redoc by default, both built from the generated OpenAPI schema.
In a default FastAPI app, at which path is the raw OpenAPI schema served as JSON?
/openapi.json
/schema.json
/docs.json
/swagger.json
The schema is generated from your routes and models and exposed at /openapi.json; /docs and /redoc read from it.
A FastAPI route is declared as @app.get('/items/{item_id}') with def read_item(item_id: int). What does GET /items/abc return?
A 422 validation error response
A 400 Bad Request response
A 404 Not Found response
A 500 Internal Server Error response
FastAPI validates path parameters against the type hint; 'abc' is not an int, so it returns 422 with details of the failed field.
In FastAPI, the route @app.get('/items/') has the handler def list_items(skip: int = 0). How is skip read from the request?
As a query parameter
As a path parameter
As a request body field
As an HTTP header
Function parameters of simple types that are not part of the path are treated as query parameters, here ?skip=10.
In FastAPI, a POST handler has the parameter item: Item, where Item subclasses Pydantic BaseModel. Where does FastAPI read item from?
The JSON request body
The URL query string
Multipart form data fields
A request cookie
Parameters typed as Pydantic models are interpreted as the request body and parsed from JSON.
With Pydantic v2 in its default (lax) mode, class User(BaseModel): age: int. What does User(age='5').age give?
The integer 5
The string '5'
The float 5.0
A ValidationError
In lax mode Pydantic coerces a numeric string to int. Strict mode (strict=True) would reject it instead.
In Pydantic v2, a model field is declared as name: Optional[str] with no default value. How does the model treat this field?
It is required but may be None
It is optional and defaults to None
It is optional and defaults to ''
It raises an error at class creation
Pydantic v2 changed this: Optional[str] only allows None as a value. Without a default the field is still required; write = None to make it optional.
A FastAPI endpoint has response_model=UserOut, where UserOut has no password field, and returns a dict that includes 'password'. What happens?
The password key is left out of the response
FastAPI raises a response validation error
The password is sent unchanged to the client
The password value is sent as null in the JSON
response_model validates and filters the output to the declared fields, which is a common way to avoid leaking secrets.
Inside an async def FastAPI endpoint, the code calls time.sleep(5). What is the effect?
It blocks the event loop and stalls other requests
FastAPI moves the blocking call to a thread pool
Python turns it into a non-blocking sleep automatically
Only this response waits, and other requests proceed
Blocking calls inside async def run on the event loop thread. Use await asyncio.sleep() or a plain def endpoint for blocking work.
How does FastAPI run a path operation declared with plain def instead of async def?
In a thread pool, so it does not block the loop
Directly on the event loop thread, like async code
In a new process for each request
It refuses to start: handlers must be async
FastAPI runs sync handlers in an external thread pool and awaits them, so blocking I/O there does not freeze the event loop.
Inside an async def function, which line pauses for one second without blocking the event loop?
await asyncio.sleep(1)
time.sleep(1)
asyncio.sleep(1)
await time.sleep(1)
asyncio.sleep must be awaited; without await it only creates a coroutine object. time.sleep blocks and is not awaitable.
A FastAPI dependency is def get_db(): db = Session(); try: yield db; finally: db.close(). When does db.close() run?
After the endpoint has finished, as cleanup
Before the endpoint function runs
Only when the endpoint raises an unhandled error
Never: yield is not allowed here
Dependencies with yield provide the value to the endpoint and run the code after yield as teardown once the endpoint is done.
In FastAPI, two sub-dependencies of one endpoint both use Depends(get_settings). By default, how many times is get_settings called per request?
Once, the result is reused
Twice, once for each use
Once for the whole app lifetime
Zero, it must be called by hand
FastAPI caches a dependency's result within a single request (use_cache=True). It is called again on the next request.
In FastAPI tests, which line replaces the get_db dependency with fake_db for every route?
app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = fake_db
app.state.dependency_overrides[get_db] = fake_db
app.dependencies[get_db] = fake_db
Depends.overrides[get_db] = fake_db
app.dependency_overrides is a dict that maps the original dependency to its replacement; clear it after the test.
In FastAPI, how do you make verify_token run for every route of one APIRouter?
APIRouter(dependencies=[Depends(verify_token)])
APIRouter(middleware=[verify_token])
APIRouter(before=[Depends(verify_token)])
APIRouter(guards=[verify_token])
Routers (and the app) accept a dependencies list that is applied to every path operation they include.
A FastAPI endpoint calls background_tasks.add_task(write_log, 'done') and returns. When does write_log run?
After the response has been sent
Before the response is sent
In a separate Celery worker
At the start of the next request
BackgroundTasks run in the same process after the response is returned, so the client does not wait for them.
A FastAPI app must run hour-long video encoding jobs with retries that survive server restarts. Which tool fits best?
A task queue such as Celery
FastAPI BackgroundTasks
An async def endpoint
A dependency with yield
BackgroundTasks live in the web process and are lost on restart. Long, retryable jobs need a separate queue and workers.
Which call correctly schedules send_email(to, subject='Hi') with FastAPI BackgroundTasks?
background_tasks.add_task(send_email, to, subject='Hi')
background_tasks.add_task(send_email(to, subject='Hi'))
background_tasks.run(send_email, to, subject='Hi')
await background_tasks.add_task(send_email, to)
add_task takes the function itself plus its arguments. Writing send_email(...) inside would run it immediately and pass its result.
In FastAPI, what does adding tags=['users'] to @app.get('/me') do?
Groups the route under 'users' in the docs
Limits the route to users with that role
Adds the /users prefix to the path
Caches the response under that tag
Tags only affect the OpenAPI schema, where Swagger UI and ReDoc group operations by tag.
A FastAPI route is declared with @app.get('/internal', include_in_schema=False). What is the result?
It works but is hidden from the docs
It is disabled and returns 404
It requires authentication to call
It only accepts requests from localhost
include_in_schema=False removes the operation from the OpenAPI schema, so it disappears from /docs, but the route still responds.
django: In Django's MVT pattern, which part receives the request, gets the data and chooses what to return, usually as a function or class?
Views hold the request handling logic. Models describe data, templates render it, and the URLconf only maps URLs to views.
In Django, what does Book.objects.filter(title='Dune') return when no book matches?
filter() always returns a QuerySet, which may be empty. Only get() raises DoesNotExist.
In Django, what happens when Book.objects.get(pk=999) finds no matching row?
get() expects exactly one row: none raises DoesNotExist and several raise MultipleObjectsReturned.
In Django, the line qs = Book.objects.filter(year=2020) runs. When is the SQL query sent to the database?
When qs is evaluated, e.g. iterated
Immediately, on that same line of code
When the model class is imported
QuerySets are lazy: building and chaining them does not hit the database until they are iterated, sliced with a step, or converted to a list.
In Django, which QuerySet method loads each book's ForeignKey author in the same SQL query using a JOIN?
select_related follows single-valued relations with a JOIN. prefetch_related runs a separate query and joins the results in Python.
Why is Product.objects.filter(pk=1).update(stock=F('stock') - 1) safer than reading stock in Python and saving it back?
The math runs in one SQL UPDATE, so concurrent updates are not lost
F() locks the whole table until the request ends, blocking other writers
F() caches the value in Python so the database is not queried again
update() retries the save automatically when it detects a conflict
F expressions refer to the column value in the database, so the decrement happens atomically in SQL instead of in a read-modify-write cycle.
In Django Admin, which ModelAdmin option sets the columns shown on a model's change list page?
list_display lists the fields shown as columns. list_filter adds the sidebar filters and fieldsets lays out the edit form.
Which command creates a user who can log in to the Django Admin with all permissions?
createsuperuser creates a user with is_staff and is_superuser set, which is what the admin site requires.
A Django view is decorated with @login_required. What happens when an anonymous user opens it?
They get a 404 Not Found page
They see the page as a guest
login_required redirects to settings.LOGIN_URL with a next parameter so the user returns to the page after logging in.
In Django 2.0 and later, which expression checks inside a view whether the current user is logged in?
is_authenticated is a boolean attribute since Django 2.0; calling it like a method raises a TypeError.
You added a new field to a Django model. Which commands create and then apply the database change?
makemigrations writes a migration file from model changes; migrate applies pending migrations to the database.
You add a non-nullable field with no default to a Django model whose table already has rows, then run makemigrations. What happens?
Django asks for a one-off default or to quit
Django silently fills the rows with NULL
Django skips the field without a warning
Existing rows need a value, so makemigrations prompts you to give a one-off default for them or to exit and add a default in the model.
Which command unapplies every migration of app shop that came after 0003_add_price?
Passing an app label and a migration name to migrate moves the app's schema to that state, unapplying later migrations.
A Django project has MIDDLEWARE = [A, B, C]. In which order do they process the response on the way out?
Middleware works like layers: requests pass top to bottom and responses pass back bottom to top.
In Django function middleware def mw(get_response): def m(request): ...; return m, what must m do to pass the request on to the view?
Call get_response(request) and return its result
Call next(request) and return nothing to the caller
Return the request object itself to the framework
Yield the request to the next layer of middleware
get_response calls the next middleware or the view; m must return the response, optionally after changing it.
A Django POST form is missing {% csrf_token %} and CsrfViewMiddleware is enabled. What does submitting it return?
CsrfViewMiddleware rejects unsafe requests without a valid token with a 403 CSRF verification failed page.
In a Django form, after form.is_valid() returns True, where do you read the cleaned and converted values?
cleaned_data holds converted Python values. form.data is the raw submitted input, and validated_data belongs to DRF serializers.
In a Django Form, which method name adds custom validation for a field called email?
Django calls clean_<fieldname>() after the field's own validation; it must return the cleaned value or raise ValidationError.
In Django REST Framework, after serializer.is_valid() returns True, where is the validated input?
validated_data holds the deserialized, validated input. initial_data is the raw input and cleaned_data is the Django forms name.
Which Django REST Framework permission class allows reads for everyone but writes only for logged-in users?
IsAuthenticatedOrReadOnly permits safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) for anyone and requires authentication for the rest. The Django model and object permission classes require login even for reads.
flask: Why is Flask usually created as app = Flask(__name__)?
So Flask can find templates and static files
So the app is named after the server it runs on
So Flask turns on debug mode for this module
So routes in the module are registered automatically
The import name tells Flask where the application module lives, which it uses to locate resources such as templates and static files.
A Flask route is @app.route('/user/<int:user_id>'). What does a request to /user/abc return?
404 Not Found
400 Bad Request
422 Unprocessable Entity
500 Server Error
The int converter only matches digits, so no route matches the URL and Flask returns 404.
Which HTTP methods does a Flask route accept when @app.route('/') is given no methods argument?
GET (with HEAD and OPTIONS added)
GET and POST (with HEAD added)
All HTTP methods, including DELETE
POST only (with OPTIONS added)
By default a route handles GET; Flask adds HEAD and OPTIONS automatically. Other methods need methods=[...].
A Flask view def profile(username) is routed at '/user/<username>'. What does url_for('profile', username='ann') return?
/user/ann
/profile/ann
/profile?username=ann
/user?username=ann
url_for takes the endpoint name (by default the function name) and fills in the route variables.
A Flask route is defined as @app.route('/projects/'). What happens when a user visits /projects without the slash?
Flask redirects to /projects/
Flask returns 404 Not Found
Flask serves it with no redirect
Flask returns 405 Not Allowed
A route with a trailing slash acts like a folder: Flask redirects the slashless URL to it. A route without one returns 404 for a URL with a trailing slash.
What is the main benefit of the Flask application factory pattern, def create_app(config): ... return app?
Several app instances with different configs, e.g. for tests
Routes are compiled ahead of time, so requests are handled faster
The app can run in production without any WSGI server
Blueprints no longer need to be registered on the app
Creating the app inside a function avoids a global app object, so tests and environments can each build an app with their own settings.
With the Flask application factory pattern, how should Flask-SQLAlchemy be set up?
db = SQLAlchemy() globally, then db.init_app(app) in create_app
db = SQLAlchemy(app) globally, before create_app runs at startup
db = SQLAlchemy() created again inside every view
db.register(app) called once from a blueprint
Creating the extension unbound and calling init_app inside the factory lets one extension object serve any app instance.
A Flask blueprint is Blueprint('auth', __name__, url_prefix='/auth') with @bp.route('/login') on def login(). Once registered, what URL serves login?
/auth/login
/login
/auth.login
/login/auth
The url_prefix given to the blueprint is prepended to all of its routes.
A view def login() lives in a Flask blueprint named 'auth'. Which call builds its URL?
url_for('auth.login')
url_for('login')
url_for('auth/login')
url_for('auth_login')
Blueprint endpoints are namespaced as blueprint_name.function_name. Inside the same blueprint, url_for('.login') also works.
Which call attaches a Flask blueprint bp to the application?
app.register_blueprint(bp)
app.add_blueprint(bp)
app.include_router(bp)
bp.register_on(app)
register_blueprint records the blueprint's routes, handlers and templates on the app, optionally with a url_prefix.
A standalone Flask script calls db.create_all() and fails with 'Working outside of application context'. Which change fixes it?
Run the call inside with app.app_context():
Import current_app at the top of the script
Set app.config['CONTEXT'] = True
Run the script with FLASK_DEBUG=1
Outside a request, nothing pushes an app context automatically. app.app_context() pushes one so current_app and extensions work.
How long does data stored on Flask's g object live?
For one application context, usually one request
For the whole lifetime of the worker process
For the user's whole session, across many requests
Until the server is restarted or redeployed
g is tied to the application context and is reset for each request, so it suits per-request data like a database connection.
Where does Flask's built-in session store its data by default?
In a signed cookie in the browser
In server memory per worker
In the configured database
In an encrypted server-side file
The default session is a cookie signed with SECRET_KEY: users cannot modify it but can read it, so do not store secrets in it.
A Flask view calls render_template('page.html', name='hi') and the template contains {{ name }}. What is output?
The escaped text <b>hi</b>
The bold word hi, rendered as HTML
An empty string, since tags are stripped
A TemplateSyntaxError from Jinja2
Flask enables Jinja2 autoescaping for .html templates. Use the |safe filter or Markup only for trusted HTML.
Which Jinja2 tag in a child template reuses base.html as its layout, so the child can override its blocks?
{% extends 'base.html' %}
{% include 'base.html' %}
{% import 'base.html' %}
{% inherit 'base.html' %}
extends sets up template inheritance with overridable blocks; include only inserts another template's output in place.
What does the Jinja2 expression {{ [3, 1, 2]|sort|first }} render?
Filters are chained left to right with the pipe: sort gives [1, 2, 3] and first takes its first item, 1.
Inside a Jinja2 loop {% for x in items %}, what is the value of loop.index on the first iteration?
None
loop.index counts from 1. loop.index0 is the zero-based counter.
Which Flask config key sets the database connection string for Flask-SQLAlchemy?
SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI
DATABASE_URL
SQLALCHEMY_URL
SQLALCHEMY_CONNECTION
Flask-SQLAlchemy reads SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI, for example sqlite:///app.db or a PostgreSQL URL.
In Flask-SQLAlchemy, after db.session.add(user), which call makes the new row permanent in the database?
db.session.commit()
db.session.flush()
db.session.refresh(user)
db.session.save()
add() only stages the object. flush() sends SQL inside the open transaction, but only commit() makes it permanent.
In Flask 1.1 and later, what does a view that returns ({'ok': False}, 400) send to the client?
A JSON response with status 400
A 200 response with the tuple as text
A TypeError and a 500 response
An HTML page that shows the dict
Since Flask 1.1, a returned dict is converted to JSON automatically, and a tuple's second item sets the status code.
spring-boot: Which three annotations does @SpringBootApplication combine?
@Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @ComponentScan
@Component, @EnableWebMvc, @ComponentScan
@Configuration, @EnableTransactionManagement, @ComponentScan
@Service, @EnableAutoConfiguration, @Import
@SpringBootApplication marks a configuration class, turns on auto-configuration and scans the package of that class and its subpackages.
Why is constructor injection recommended over field injection with @Autowired in Spring?
Dependencies can be final and are easy to pass in tests
It is the only injection Spring Boot supports
It makes beans load lazily on first use
It avoids the need for any @Component annotations
Constructor injection makes required dependencies explicit, allows immutable fields and lets unit tests create the class without Spring.
Two beans implement PaymentService. Which annotation on one of them makes Spring inject it by default when no qualifier is given?
@Primary
@Qualifier
@Default
@Preferred
@Primary marks the preferred candidate among several beans of the same type. @Qualifier is used to pick a bean by name at the injection point.
What is the default scope of a Spring bean declared with @Component?
Singleton
Prototype
Request
Session
By default the container creates one shared instance per bean definition. Prototype creates a new instance for each injection.
In Spring MVC, what does @RestController add compared to @Controller?
Return values are written to the response body
Endpoints get REST security by default
Methods are mapped to REST verbs by name
Responses are cached on the server
@RestController is @Controller plus @ResponseBody, so returned objects are serialized (for example to JSON) instead of resolved as view names.
For GET /users/42?active=true and @GetMapping("/users/{id}"), which annotation binds 42 to the Long id parameter?
@PathVariable
@RequestParam
@RequestBody
@RequestHeader
@PathVariable binds a URI template variable; @RequestParam would bind the active query parameter.
A Spring MVC handler has the parameter @RequestParam String q with no other attributes. What happens when a request has no q parameter?
The request fails with 400 Bad Request
q is set to null and the handler runs
q is set to an empty string instead
The request fails with 500 Internal Server Error
@RequestParam is required by default; a missing value triggers MissingServletRequestParameterException, mapped to 400. Use required = false or a default value.
In Spring Data JPA, UserRepository extends JpaRepository<User, Long> declares List<User> findByLastNameAndAge(String lastName, int age). What does this do?
Spring derives a query filtering by both fields
It fails at startup until you write an @Query
It loads all users and filters them in Java
It creates a new database index on both columns
Spring Data parses derived query method names and generates the query at startup, with no implementation needed.
In Spring Data JPA, what is the return type of findById(id) on a JpaRepository<User, Long>?
Optional<User>
User, or null
List<User>
ResponseEntity<User>
findById returns Optional so callers must handle the missing case, for example with orElseThrow().
By default, a Spring @Transactional method rolls back when it throws which kind of exception?
Unchecked ones (RuntimeException, Error)
Any exception, whether checked or unchecked
Only checked exceptions such as IOException
Only SQLException and its subclasses
Checked exceptions commit by default. Use rollbackFor to roll back on them too.
In a Spring bean, method a() calls this.b(), and only b() is annotated with @Transactional. Why does b() run without a new transaction?
The self-call skips the Spring proxy
@Transactional only works on interfaces
b() must be declared static
Transactions need XML configuration
Spring applies @Transactional through a proxy. A call on this inside the same object never goes through the proxy, so the advice is not applied.
In JPA, what is the default fetch type of a @ManyToOne association?
EAGER
LAZY
SUBSELECT
BATCH
The JPA spec makes to-one associations EAGER and to-many associations LAZY by default; many teams set @ManyToOne to LAZY explicitly.
You add spring-boot-starter-web to a Spring Boot app. What does auto-configuration provide without extra code?
An embedded Tomcat and Spring MVC setup
A configured H2 database and JPA repositories
A login page protecting all endpoints
A Thymeleaf template engine for views
Auto-configuration reacts to the classpath: the web starter brings Tomcat and Spring MVC, which Boot then configures with sensible defaults.
In a Spring Boot app, you declare your own DataSource @Bean. What happens to Boot's auto-configured DataSource?
It backs off and yours is used
Both are created, causing an error
Boot's bean overrides yours
Boot merges the two configurations
Most auto-configurations use @ConditionalOnMissingBean, so a user-defined bean of the same type replaces the default.
Which property in application.properties changes the HTTP port of a Spring Boot web app?
server.port
spring.port
server.http.port
spring.web.port
server.port sets the embedded server port; the default is 8080.
A Spring Boot app has application-dev.yml next to application.yml. Which setting makes Boot load the dev file?
spring.profiles.active=dev
spring.config.dev=true
spring.application.profile=dev
server.profile=dev
Profile-specific files application-{profile}.yml are loaded on top of application.yml for each active profile.
application.properties has server.port=9090 and the app starts with --server.port=7000 on the command line. Which port is used?
Command-line arguments have higher precedence than application.properties in Spring Boot's externalized configuration.
You add spring-boot-starter-security to a Spring Boot app with no security configuration. What happens?
Every endpoint requires login with a generated password
Nothing changes until you add a SecurityFilterChain bean
Only POST and PUT endpoints require authentication
The app refuses to start without a configured user store
Security auto-configuration protects all endpoints and creates a user named 'user' whose random password is printed in the log at startup.
Which Spring Security PasswordEncoder is the appropriate choice for storing user passwords?
BCryptPasswordEncoder
NoOpPasswordEncoder
Base64PasswordEncoder
LdapShaPasswordEncoder
BCrypt is an adaptive, salted hash designed for passwords. NoOp stores plain text, and LdapSha is deprecated legacy support.
In Spring Security 6, how do you configure which HTTP endpoints require authentication?
Declare a SecurityFilterChain @Bean
Extend WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter
Add security rules to web.xml
Annotate controllers with @Secure
WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter was deprecated in 5.7 and removed in 6.0; configuration now uses a SecurityFilterChain bean built from HttpSecurity.
ruby-on-rails: Following Rails conventions, which database table does the Active Record model class Person map to?
people
persons
person
person_table
Rails pluralizes the class name using its inflector, which knows irregular plurals like person to people.
In Rails, which controller class handles requests for the routes created by resources :articles?
ArticlesController
ArticleController
Articles::Controller
ArticlesResource
Controller names are the plural resource name plus Controller, in app/controllers/articles_controller.rb.
A Rails ArticlesController#index action has no explicit render call. What does Rails render?
app/views/articles/index.html.erb
app/views/index.html.erb
app/views/layouts/articles.html.erb
Nothing, it returns 204
By convention Rails renders the template named after the controller and action when the action does not render or redirect.
What does bin/rails generate migration AddPriceToProducts price:decimal create?
A migration that adds a price column to products
A new Price model with its table
A migration creating an add_price table
A Products controller with a price action
The AddXxxToYyy name pattern tells the generator to write add_column :products, :price, :decimal.
Which command reverts the most recently applied migration in Rails?
bin/rails db:rollback
bin/rails db:migrate:undo
bin/rails db:revert
bin/rails db:reset
db:rollback undoes the last migration (STEP=n for more). db:reset drops and recreates the whole database.
In Rails 5 and later, class Book < ApplicationRecord has belongs_to :author. What happens when you save a book with no author?
Validation fails: Author must exist
It saves with author_id set to NULL
The database raises a NOT NULL error
Rails creates an empty author record
Since Rails 5, belongs_to is required by default. Add optional: true to allow a missing association.
A Rails Post model has has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy. What happens when you call post.destroy?
Each comment is destroyed too, running callbacks
Comments stay in the table but lose their post_id
Deletion fails while any comments still exist
Comments are archived into another table first
dependent: :destroy loads and destroys each associated record. :delete_all removes them in SQL without callbacks.
In Rails, Post has_many :comments and Comment belongs_to :post. Where is the foreign key stored?
post_id column in the comments table
comment_id column in the posts table
A posts_comments join table
Both tables, one id each
The model with belongs_to holds the foreign key, so the comments table gets a post_id column.
Which Rails association models a many-to-many relation through a join model that has its own attributes and validations?
has_many :through
has_and_belongs_to_many
has_one :through
belongs_to :through
has_many :through uses a real model for the join table. has_and_belongs_to_many uses a bare join table with no model.
With resources :photos in config/routes.rb, which request is routed to PhotosController#destroy?
DELETE /photos/:id
POST /photos/:id/destroy
GET /photos/:id/delete
DELETE /photos
Resourceful routes map HTTP verbs to actions: DELETE on a member URL goes to destroy.
In Rails routes, what does root 'pages#home' do?
Maps / to the home action of PagesController
Maps /pages to the home action
Makes PagesController the parent of all routes
Redirects /home to the pages index
root defines the route for the path / using the controller#action string.
Which command lists every route of a Rails app with its verb, path and controller action?
bin/rails routes
bin/rails routes:list
bin/rails show:routes
bin/rails about
bin/rails routes prints the routing table; you can filter it, for example with -c articles.
In a Rails controller, User.new(params[:user]) is called without strong parameters. What happens?
It raises ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesError
All submitted attributes are assigned to the user
Only the string attributes are assigned, others dropped
The user is built with no attributes and no error
Rails refuses unpermitted mass assignment. Use params.require(:user).permit(:name, :email).
A Rails controller declares before_action :set_article, only: [:show, :edit]. When does set_article run?
Before the show and edit actions only
Before every action in the controller
After the show and edit actions
Once, when the controller loads
Callbacks with only: run for the listed actions. except: does the reverse.
In a Rails create action, why use render :new instead of redirect_to new_article_path when @article.save fails?
render keeps @article and its errors for the form
render runs the new action again before showing it
redirect_to cannot be used after a failed save
render forces the browser to reload the form page
render only renders a template within the same request, so the invalid object and its error messages stay available. A redirect starts a new request.
In Rails, a controller sets flash[:notice] = 'Saved' and then calls redirect_to. How long is the message available?
For the next request only
For the current request only
For the whole user session
Until it is cleared by hand
The flash survives exactly one request after it is set, which fits messages shown after a redirect. flash.now is for the current request.
Why does the Rails asset pipeline add a digest to file names, as in application-3f2a9c.css?
So browsers cache files long-term but fetch new versions
So the asset files are encrypted on the server at rest
So files uploaded by different users do not collide
So assets load in alphabetical order on every page
Fingerprinting changes the URL whenever the content changes, allowing far-future cache headers without serving stale files.
In a Rails layout, which helper outputs a link tag pointing to the fingerprinted application stylesheet?
stylesheet_link_tag 'application'
css_include_tag 'application'
asset_link 'application.css'
link_stylesheet 'application'
stylesheet_link_tag resolves the asset path through the pipeline, including the digest in production.
In RESTful Rails routing with resources :articles, which action handles PATCH /articles/5?
update
edit
create
replace
PATCH (and PUT) on a member URL map to update. GET /articles/5/edit maps to edit, which only shows the form.
With resources :posts do resources :comments end, what is the path to the comments index of one post?
/posts/:post_id/comments
/comments?post_id=:post_id
/posts/comments/:id
/post/:id/comments
Nested resources put the parent id in the URL as :post_id, which the controller reads as params[:post_id].
laravel: Which Artisan command creates a new controller class named PostController?
make:* commands generate classes; make:controller places the file in app/Http/Controllers.
Which Artisan command starts a local development server for a Laravel app?
serve starts PHP's built-in server, by default on http://127.0.0.1:8000. artisan up only ends maintenance mode.
Which Artisan command prints all registered routes with their methods, URIs and actions?
route:list displays the route table and can filter, for example with --path=api.
By Laravel convention, which table does the Eloquent model class OrderItem use when no $table is set?
Eloquent uses the snake_case plural of the class name unless the model sets $table.
A Laravel model has neither $fillable nor $guarded set. What does Post::create($request->all()) do?
It saves only the id and timestamps
It silently saves an empty row
Models are fully guarded by default ($guarded = ['*']). List allowed attributes in $fillable to enable mass assignment.
A Laravel User model has public function posts() { return $this->hasMany(Post::class); }. What is the difference between $user->posts and $user->posts()?
The property gives the loaded Collection, the method a query builder
The property gives a query builder, the method the Collection
Both return the same Collection object, so either works
The property only works after save() is called on the user
The dynamic property runs the query and returns results. The method returns the relation, so you can chain constraints like ->where(...)->get().
A Blade view loops over posts and prints $post->author->name, causing one query per post. Which fix loads authors up front?
with() eager loads the relation in one extra query, solving the N+1 problem.
In a Laravel controller, Post::findOrFail(999) finds no row. What does the user get by default?
A null value passed to the view
A redirect to the home page
findOrFail throws ModelNotFoundException, which Laravel's exception handler turns into a 404 response.
Which Blade syntax prints a variable without HTML escaping?
{{ }} escapes output with htmlspecialchars. {!! !!} prints raw HTML, so use it only for trusted content.
In a Blade layout file, which directive marks where a child view's @section('content') is inserted?
Layouts declare @yield placeholders; child views use @extends and fill them with @section.
A Blade form posts to a route in the web middleware group but has no @csrf directive. What status does Laravel return?
Laravel's CSRF middleware rejects the request and returns its 419 Page Expired error. @csrf adds the hidden _token field.
A Laravel route is defined with Route::get('/profile', ...)->name('profile'). Which helper generates its URL?
route() builds a URL from a named route, so URLs stay correct even if the path changes later.
With Route::resource('photos', PhotoController::class), which controller method handles GET /photos/{photo}/edit?
Resource routes map GET /photos/{photo}/edit to edit (show the form) and PUT/PATCH /photos/{photo} to update.
Routes are wrapped in Route::middleware('auth')->group(...). What happens when a guest requests one of them in a browser?
They are redirected to the login route
They get a 404 Not Found page
They see the page as a guest
They get a 500 Server Error page
The auth middleware redirects unauthenticated browser requests to the login route; JSON requests get a 401 instead.
In a new Laravel 11 application, where do you register middleware aliases?
Laravel 11 removed the HTTP Kernel from new apps; middleware is configured in bootstrap/app.php. Kernel.php was used in Laravel 10 and earlier.
In the Laravel service container, how does $this->app->singleton(Cache::class, ...) differ from $this->app->bind(Cache::class, ...)?
singleton resolves the same instance every time
singleton creates a new instance every time
bind runs the factory on each resolve; singleton runs it once and then reuses the result.
According to the Laravel docs, in which service provider method should you only bind things into the container?
register() runs before all providers are booted, so it should only bind. boot() runs later and can use other registered services.
A Laravel controller constructor type-hints PaymentGateway, an interface bound to StripeGateway in a provider. What does Laravel pass in?
A StripeGateway instance from the container
null, until you call app()->make() yourself
An error: interfaces cannot be injected
The container resolves controller dependencies automatically and uses the binding to choose the concrete class.
Which Artisan command reverts the last batch of migrations in Laravel?
Migrations run in batches; migrate:rollback undoes the latest batch, and --step=n rolls back a set number of migrations.
Which Artisan command drops all tables, runs every migration again and then runs the seeders?
migrate:fresh drops all tables and migrates from scratch; --seed then runs DatabaseSeeder.
dotnet: What does the C# compiler produce from your source code in .NET?
IL code that the CLR JIT-compiles at runtime
Native machine code for one specific CPU only
JavaScript that runs in a bundled V8 engine
Java bytecode that runs on the JVM
C# compiles to Intermediate Language in assemblies; the CLR's JIT turns it into native code when it runs (AOT is an optional alternative).
In the .NET garbage collector, in which generation are most newly allocated small objects placed?
Generation 0
Generation 1
Generation 2
The Large Object Heap
New objects start in gen 0, which is collected often. Survivors are promoted to gen 1 and gen 2. Very large objects go to the LOH.
In C#, given struct P { public int X; }, what does var a = new P { X = 1 }; var b = a; b.X = 2; Console.WriteLine(a.X); print?
null
Structs are value types, so assigning a to b copies it. Changing b does not affect a. With a class it would print 2.
In C#, var list = new List<int> { 1, 2 }; var q = list.Where(x => x > 1); list.Add(5); What does q.Count() return?
LINQ queries use deferred execution: Where runs when q is enumerated, after 5 was added, so it matches 2 and 5.
What does the [ApiController] attribute do when an ASP.NET Core action receives a model that fails validation?
It returns 400 with the validation errors
It passes the invalid model to the action
It returns 422 with an empty body
It throws an exception and returns 500
[ApiController] checks ModelState automatically and returns a 400 ValidationProblemDetails response before the action runs.
In an ASP.NET Core controller action returning ActionResult<Product>, what does return NotFound(); send?
A 404 status code
A 204 status code
A 400 status code
A null JSON body with 200
NotFound() creates a NotFoundResult, which produces a 404 response.
In an ASP.NET Core minimal API, what does app.MapGet("/hello", () => "Hi"); return for GET /hello?
The text Hi as text/plain
The JSON string "Hi"
An HTML page saying Hi
An empty 204 response
Minimal APIs write a returned string as text/plain; other returned objects are serialized to JSON.
An ASP.NET Core action has [HttpGet("items/{id:int}")]. What does a request to items/abc return?
404 Not Found
400 Bad Request
500 Server Error
200 with id = 0
Route constraints affect matching: 'abc' fails the int constraint, so no endpoint matches and the result is 404.
In ASP.NET Core, a service is registered with builder.Services.AddScoped<IRepo, Repo>(). How many Repo instances are created?
One per HTTP request
One for the whole application
A new one per injection
One per worker thread
Scoped services live for one scope, which in ASP.NET Core is one request. Singleton is one for the app and transient is new on every resolve.
In ASP.NET Core Development mode, a singleton service takes a scoped service in its constructor. What happens?
Scope validation throws an InvalidOperationException
The scoped service silently becomes a singleton for the app
A new scoped instance is made for every method call
Nothing happens, since it is a supported DI pattern
Scope validation, enabled in Development, detects this captive dependency and refuses to resolve it. Without validation it would hold one scoped instance forever.
Which commands create an EF Core migration named Initial and apply it to the database with the dotnet CLI?
dotnet ef migrations add Initial, then dotnet ef database update
dotnet ef migrate Initial, then dotnet ef apply
dotnet ef database add Initial, then dotnet ef migrations update
dotnet migrations new Initial, then dotnet database push
migrations add generates the migration code from the model; database update applies pending migrations.
What lifetime does builder.Services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>() give the DbContext by default?
Scoped
Singleton
Transient
Pooled singleton
DbContext is not thread safe and is meant to be short-lived, so AddDbContext registers it as scoped, one per request.
An EF Core query only reads data to display it and never changes it. Which call reduces its overhead?
AsNoTracking()
AsSplitQuery()
AsEnumerable()
AsTracking()
AsNoTracking skips the change tracker, which saves memory and time for read-only queries.
In EF Core, var u = ctx.Users.Find(1); u.Name = "Ann"; Which call writes the change to the database?
ctx.SaveChanges()
ctx.Users.Update()
ctx.Commit()
ctx.Entry(u).Reload()
Find returns a tracked entity, so the change tracker detects the modified property and SaveChanges issues the UPDATE.
In EF Core, which query loads blogs together with their related posts?
ctx.Blogs.Include(b => b.Posts)
ctx.Blogs.Join(b => b.Posts)
ctx.Blogs.With(b => b.Posts)
ctx.Blogs.Load(b => b.Posts)
Include performs eager loading of a navigation property in the same query (or split queries if configured).
In an ASP.NET Core Program.cs, in which order should app.UseAuthentication() and app.UseAuthorization() be called?
UseAuthentication, then UseAuthorization
UseAuthorization, then UseAuthentication
Either order, they are independent
Only one of them may be called
Middleware runs in registration order. Authorization needs the user identity that authentication sets up first.
In ASP.NET Core, a middleware app.Use(async (ctx, next) => { await ctx.Response.WriteAsync("x"); }) never calls next. What happens?
Later middleware and endpoints do not run
The pipeline calls next automatically
An exception is thrown at startup
Only the endpoint still runs afterward
Not calling next short-circuits the pipeline, which is how middleware such as static files ends a request early.
An ASP.NET Core app sets Logging:LogLevel:Default in appsettings.json and also as an environment variable. Which value wins by default?
The environment variable
The appsettings.json value
Whichever key is read first
Startup fails with a conflict
The default builder adds providers in order: appsettings.json, appsettings.{Environment}.json, user secrets, environment variables, command line. Later ones win.
Which environment variable name sets the configuration key ConnectionStrings:Default in ASP.NET Core on all platforms?
ConnectionStrings__Default
ConnectionStrings:Default
ConnectionStrings.Default
CONNECTIONSTRINGS_DEFAULT
A double underscore is replaced with the colon separator, and it works on every OS, unlike a colon in variable names.
After builder.Services.Configure<SmtpOptions>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("Smtp")), what should a service inject to read the settings?
IOptions<SmtpOptions>
SmtpOptions directly
IConfiguration<SmtpOptions>
ISettings<SmtpOptions>
The options pattern exposes bound settings through IOptions<T> (or IOptionsSnapshot / IOptionsMonitor for reloadable values).
